components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored value must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+' (e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be
            valid for the owner's city per a fixed table keyed by the city's region
            ('Sydney' -> NSW 2000-2099, 'Melbourne' -> VIC 3000-3099, 'Brisbane' ->
            QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
            A postcode that is malformed or out of range for the city's region is
            rejected with a 400. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is used to derive the owner's 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Optional create-time directive. When true, the owner is permitted to
            share a household with an existing owner, so the create request is not
            rejected as a household duplicate even when another owner has the same
            last name and postcode. A declared household member is created and is
            not flagged as a possible duplicate.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region), derived by preferring the postcode: a 4-digit
                postcode within a known region's range ('NSW' 2000-2099, 'VIC' 3000-3099,
                'QLD' 4000-4099) yields that region. When the postcode is absent or in no known
                range, it falls back to a fixed city-to-region table ('Sydney' -> 'NSW',
                'Melbourne' -> 'VIC', 'Brisbane' -> 'QLD'). A city not in the table with no
                region-bearing postcode derives the locality 'UNKNOWN'.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code

## Summary

I implemented `telephoneDisplay` — the stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans — while keeping `telephone` as raw E.164. Three coordinated changes:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a `telephoneDisplay` read-only string property to the `Owner` response schema (alongside the other derived fields like `displayName`/`initials`). Since DTOs are generated by openapi-generator at build time, this adds the field to `OwnerDto`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`** — Added a pure `toDisplay(String)` method that normalizes the stored value, splits off the country code using the existing `NATIONAL_LENGTH_BY_COUNTRY_CODE` prefix table, and renders `+<cc> <national digits grouped in threes>` (e.g. `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678`). Unrecognized country codes or non-E.164 legacy values are returned unchanged so the raw form is never lost. Added a small `groupInThrees` helper for the digit grouping.

3. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a MapStruct `@Mapping` on `toOwnerDto` that populates `telephoneDisplay` from `owner.getTelephone()` via `TelephoneNormalizer.toDisplay`, following the same derived-field expression pattern already used for `displayName`, `locality`, etc.

## Summary

I implemented `telephoneDisplay` — the stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans — while keeping `telephone` as raw E.164. Three coordinated changes:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a `telephoneDisplay` read-only string property to the `Owner` response schema (alongside the other derived fields like `displayName`/`initials`). Since DTOs are generated by openapi-generator at build time, this adds the field to `OwnerDto`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`** — Added a pure `toDisplay(String)` method that normalizes the stored value, splits off the country code using the existing `NATIONAL_LENGTH_BY_COUNTRY_CODE` prefix table, and renders `+<cc> <national digits grouped in threes>` (e.g. `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678`). Unrecognized country codes or non-E.164 legacy values are returned unchanged so the raw form is never lost. Added a small `groupInThrees` helper for the digit grouping.

3. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a MapStruct `@Mapping` on `toOwnerDto` that populates `telephoneDisplay` from `owner.getTelephone()` via `TelephoneNormalizer.toDisplay`, following the same derived-field expression pattern already used for `displayName`, `locality`, etc.
